def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categor:
## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring and let $\delta\in R$. A set partition of a finite set is a collection of disjoint nonempty subsets, called blocks, whose union is the whole set; a perfect matching is a set partition whose blocks each have size two. For $a,b\in\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$, place $a$ ordered input vertices on a top edge and $b$ ordered output vertices on a bottom edge. The Brauer module $\mathcal B_\delta(a,b)$ is the free $R$-module on perfect matchings of these $a+b$ vertices. It is zero if $a+b$ is odd. The partition module $\mathcal P_\delta(a,b)$ is the free $R$-module on set partitions of the same vertices.

For $D\in\mathcal B_\delta(a,b)$ and $E\in\mathcal B_\delta(b,c)$, glue the output vertices of $D$ to the corresponding input vertices of $E$. Take the equivalence relation generated by the two matchings and these identifications. Each equivalence class meeting an outer vertex consists of exactly two outer vertices and gives an edge of a new matching. Each class meeting no outer vertex is a closed loop. Define $E\circ D=\delta^\ell H$, where $H$ is the resulting outer matching and $\ell$ is the number of removed loops. For partition diagrams use the equivalence relation generated by the two partitions and the same gluing; each outer equivalence class gives a block and each class with no outer vertices contributes one factor $\delta$. Extend composition $R$-bilinearly.

The identity at $a$ is the matching joining input $i$ to output $i$, respectively the partition into those $a$ through-blocks. Juxtaposition defines tensor product on objects by addition and on diagrams by disjoint union. The Brauer algebra $B_a(\delta)$ and partition algebra $P_a(\delta)$ are the endomorphism algebras at object $a$.

These are abstract diagram modules over arbitrary $R$. This definition asserts no faithfulness of any tensor representation.
def-polynomial-invariants-for-a-rational:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a field. An affine algebraic group $G$ over $k$ is an affine variety with algebraic multiplication, identity, and inverse maps satisfying the group axioms. Its coordinate algebra $k[G]$ has comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, the pullbacks of multiplication and the identity map. A finite-dimensional **rational left $G$-module** is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ with a $k$-linear coaction $\lambda_V:V\to k[G]\otimes_k V$ satisfying $(\Delta\otimes\operatorname{id}_V)\lambda_V=(\operatorname{id}_{k[G]}\otimes\lambda_V)\lambda_V$ and $(\varepsilon\otimes\operatorname{id}_V)\lambda_V=\operatorname{id}_V$; equivalently it is a morphism of varieties $G\times V\to V$ defining an algebraic left action. With this left-comodule convention the left action is recovered by $g\cdot v=(\operatorname{ev}_{g^{-1}}\otimes\operatorname{id}_V)\lambda_V(v)$; equivalently $\lambda_V(v)$ evaluated at $g$ is $g^{-1}\cdot v$. The inverse is necessary because evaluation of the displayed left coaction directly at $g$ gives a right action. Its affine coordinate ring is $k[V]=\operatorname{Sym}_k(V^*)$. For every integer $t\ge0$, the diagonal action on $V^t$ induces a coaction $\lambda_{k[V^t]}:k[V^t]\to k[G]\otimes_k k[V^t]$ by pullback of the action morphism. The invariant subring is
$$k[V^t]^G=\{f\in k[V^t]:\lambda_{k[V^t]}(f)=1\otimes f\}.$$
This is the algebraic-group coaction convention; it does not identify invariants of the finite group of $k$-points $G(k)$ with $k[V^t]^G$.
lem-gram-map-fibers-and-rank-strata:
## Statement

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero and let $t\ge0$. Let $V$ have dimension $m\ge1$ with a nondegenerate symmetric form $B$, or dimension $m=2n\ge2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form $B$. Symmetric means $B(v,w)=B(w,v)$; alternating means $B(v,v)=0$ for every $v$; nondegenerate means that $B(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in V$ implies $v=0$. Write $GL(V)$ for the group of invertible linear maps on $V$, and set $O(V,B)=\{g\in GL(V):B(gv,gw)=B(v,w)\}$ and, in the alternating case, $Sp(V,B)=\{g\in GL(V):B(gv,gw)=B(v,w)\}$; these denote the full isometry groups. The Gram map sends $(v_1,\ldots,v_t)\in V^t$ to $(B(v_i,v_j))_{i,j}\in\operatorname{Mat}_t(k)$. Its image is the set of symmetric, respectively alternating, matrices of rank at most $\min(m,t)$. When $t\ge m$, every Gram matrix of rank $m$ has a single fiber orbit under the stated group, and the stabilizer of each tuple in that orbit is trivial. For even $r$, let $J_r$ denote the block diagonal matrix with $r/2$ copies of $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$; let $I_r$ denote the $r\times r$ identity matrix. For $0\le r\le\min(m,t)$, the rank-$r$ symmetric stratum has dimension $rt-r(r-1)/2$; for even $0\le r\le\min(m,t)$, the rank-$r$ alternating stratum has dimension $rt-r(r+1)/2$.
lem-multilinear-minor-pfaffian-ideal-com:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a field, $t\ge1$, and $0\le m<t$. Write $[t]=\{1,\ldots,t\}$ and let $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb N^t$. In the polynomial ring on the generic symmetric $t\times t$ matrix $Z=(z_{ij})$, give $z_{ij}=z_{ji}$ multidegree $e_i+e_j$. For $I,J\subseteq[t]$ of size $m+1$, order each subset increasingly and write $Z_{I,J}$ for the corresponding minor. The multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$ component of the ideal generated by all $(m+1)$-minors is spanned by
$$\det(Z_{I,J})\prod_{\{a,b\}\in\pi}z_{ab},$$
where $I$ and $J$ are disjoint and $\pi$ is a perfect matching (a partition into two-element blocks) of $[t]\setminus(I\cup J)$. For a generic alternating $t\times t$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ with $a_{ji}=-a_{ij}$ and $a_{ii}=0$, give $a_{ij}$ multidegree $e_i+e_j$. Fix $1\le s\le\lfloor t/2\rfloor$. For $S\subseteq[t]$, let $A_S$ be the principal submatrix with indices in increasing order. The multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$ component of the ideal generated by principal Pfaffians of size $2s$ is spanned by
$$\operatorname{Pf}(A_S)\prod_{\{a,b\}\in\pi}a_{ab},$$
where $S=(s_1<\cdots<s_{2s})$ and $\pi$ is a perfect matching of $[t]\setminus S$. More precisely, for a perfect matching $M=\{\{i_1,j_1\},\ldots,\{i_s,j_s\}\}$ of $\{1,\ldots,2s\}$ (that is, a partition into two-element blocks), order each pair so $i_a<j_a$ and order the pairs by $i_1<\cdots<i_s$; set $\operatorname{sgn}(M)=\operatorname{sgn}(i_1,j_1,\ldots,i_s,j_s)$, the sign of that permutation of $\{1,\ldots,2s\}$. Then $\operatorname{Pf}(A_S)=\sum_M\operatorname{sgn}(M)\prod_{a=1}^s a_{s_{i_a},s_{j_a}}$. An empty spanning family denotes the zero subspace.
lem-even-row-tableau-generating-identity:
## Statement

Let $t\ge1$. A semistandard tableau has weakly increasing rows and strictly increasing columns. For tableaux $T$ with entries in $[t]$ and all row lengths even, let $w_i(T)$ count its entries equal to $i$. Then, as a formal power series,
$$
\sum_T\prod_{i=1}^t x_i^{w_i(T)}=\prod_{1\le i\le j\le t}(1-x_ix_j)^{-1}.
$$
In particular the number of these tableaux with $2d$ boxes is $\binom{t(t+1)/2+d-1}{d}$ for $d\ge0$.
lem-generic-symmetric-minor-straightenin:
## Statement

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, $t\ge1$, and $0\le m<t$. Let $Z=(z_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le t}$ be the generic symmetric matrix, with $z_{ij}=z_{ji}$, and let $I_{m+1}$ be the ideal generated by its $(m+1)$-minors. For increasing subsets $A=(a_1<\cdots<a_s)$ and $C=(c_1<\cdots<c_{s'})$ of $[t]$, write $A\unrhd C$ when $s\le s'$ and $a_j\ge c_j$ for every $1\le j\le s$. Let $H_t$ consist of pairs $(A,B)$ of equal-size subsets with $A\unrhd B$, including $(\varnothing,\varnothing)$, and put $(A,B)\unrhd(C,D)$ when $B\unrhd C$. Write $p(A,B)=\det Z_{A,B}$, with $p(\varnothing,\varnothing)=1$. A product $p(A_1,B_1)\cdots p(A_q,B_q)$ is standard when $(A_1,B_1)\unrhd\cdots\unrhd(A_q,B_q)$. The classes of the standard products with $|A_i|\le m$ form a $k$-basis of $k[z_{ij}]/I_{m+1}$. Every nonstandard product can be rewritten as a linear combination of standard products by the explicit determinant-coefficient identities in the proof; these rewrites terminate after a single substitution. Empty factors are discarded when indexing distinct standard products. The substitution $Z=XX^{\mathsf T}$, for a generic $t\times m$ matrix $X$, induces an injective map of this quotient into $k[x_{ic}]$. In column-first lexicographic order $x_{11}>\cdots>x_{t1}>x_{12}>\cdots>x_{tm}$, the image of $p(A,B)$ with $|A|=|B|=s\le m$ has leading monomial $\prod_{c=1}^s x_{a_cc}x_{b_cc}$ with coefficient one; distinct standard products have distinct leading monomials. If $m\ge t$, then $I_{m+1}=0$ and the quotient is the polynomial ring.
lem-generic-pfaffian-straightening:
## Statement

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, $t\ge1$, and even $m$ with $0\le m\le t$. Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be the generic alternating $t\times t$ matrix, and let $J_{m+2}$ be the ideal generated by its principal Pfaffians of size $m+2$ (zero when $m+2>t$). For $S=(s_1<\cdots<s_h)\subseteq[t]$, let $A_S$ be the principal submatrix with rows and columns in this order, and write $P_S=\operatorname{Pf}(A_S)$, with $P_\varnothing=1$. Explicitly, for $M=\{\{i_1,j_1\},\ldots,\{i_{h/2},j_{h/2}\}\}$ a perfect matching of $\{1,\ldots,h\}$, order each pair with $i_a<j_a$ and the pairs by $i_1<\cdots<i_{h/2}$; define $\operatorname{sgn}(M)=\operatorname{sgn}(i_1,j_1,\ldots,i_{h/2},j_{h/2})$, the sign of that permutation. Then $P_S=\sum_M\operatorname{sgn}(M)\prod_a a_{s_{i_a},s_{j_a}}$. For even subsets $S=(s_1<\cdots<s_h)$ and $T=(t_1<\cdots<t_{h'})$, define $P_S\preceq P_T$ if $h'\le h$ and $s_j\le t_j$ for every $1\le j\le h'$. Let $M_m=(1,\ldots,m)$, with $M_0=\varnothing$. A product $P_{S_1}\cdots P_{S_q}$ is standard if $P_{S_1}\preceq\cdots\preceq P_{S_q}$ and $P_{M_m}\preceq P_{S_1}$. Under the Gram substitution $a_{uv}\mapsto\sum_{r=1}^{m/2}(x_{u,2r-1}x_{v,2r}-x_{v,2r-1}x_{u,2r})$, the quotient embeds into $k[x_{ij}:1\le i\le t,1\le j\le m]$. For column-first lexicographic order giving earlier columns and smaller rows priority, for $|S|\le m$ the unique leading monomial of $P_S$ is $\prod_{j=1}^{|S|}x_{s_j,j}$ with coefficient one. The classes of these standard products form a $k$-basis of $k[a_{ij}:i<j]/J_{m+2}$. Every nonstandard product can be rewritten using the indexed shuffle identities in the proof, and these rewrites terminate. If $m+2>t$, the ideal is zero.
lem-brauer-and-partition-composition-is-:
## Statement

For every commutative unital ring $R$, every $\delta\in R$, and every composable triple of Brauer diagrams or of partition diagrams, the composition defined in [[def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categories]] is associative and has the stated identity diagrams as units.
lem-brauer-and-partition-diagram-basis-r:
## Statement

For $a\ge0$, the Brauer algebra $B_a(\delta)$ over any commutative unital ring $R$ is free of rank $(2a-1)!!$, with $(-1)!!=1$. The partition algebra $P_a(\delta)$ is free of rank $\operatorname{Bell}(2a)$, where $\operatorname{Bell}(j)$ denotes the number of set partitions of a $j$-element set.
lem-generic-symmetric-determinantal-ring:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Under the hypotheses and notation of [[lem-generic-symmetric-minor-straightening]], the ring $k[z_{ij}]/I_{m+1}$ is an integrally closed domain for every $0\le m\le t$.
lem-generic-pfaffian-ring-normal:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Under the hypotheses and notation of [[lem-generic-pfaffian-straightening]], the ring $k[a_{ij}:i<j]/J_{m+2}$ is an integrally closed domain for every even $m$ with $0\le m\le t$.
thm-brauer-generator-presentation:
## Statement

In the $R$-linear Brauer category of [[def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categories]], identity strands $I$, adjacent crossing $X:2\to2$, cap $A:2\to0$, and cup $U:0\to2$ generate every morphism under composition and juxtaposition. They satisfy the identity/interchange relations and
$$X^2=I^{\otimes2},\qquad (X\otimes I)(I\otimes X)(X\otimes I)=(I\otimes X)(X\otimes I)(I\otimes X),$$
$$A X=A,\qquad A U=\delta\,1_0,\qquad (A\otimes I)(I\otimes X)=(I\otimes A)(X\otimes I),$$
$$ (A\otimes I)(I\otimes U)=I. $$
The dual relations are included. A scaled Brauer diagram means an $R$-multiple of one basis matching. The claim is that these relations are complete: any two words evaluating to the same scaled Brauer diagram are equivalent using them.
lem-bmw-cubic-relation-and-hecke-quotien:
## Statement

For the convention in [[def-bmw-algebra-with-fixed-kauffman-skein-convention]], every generator satisfies $(g_i-q)(g_i+q^{-1})(g_i-\rho^{-1})=0$. In the cup-cap-zero quotient, it instead satisfies the Hecke quadratic $(g_i-q)(g_i+q^{-1})=0$.
lem-symmetric-and-alternating-rank-coord:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $t\ge1$. For each integer $0\le m\le t$, in the polynomial ring of a generic symmetric $t\times t$ matrix $Z$, the ideal $I_{m+1}$ generated by all $(m+1)$-minors is prime and its zero set is the locus $\operatorname{rank}Z\le m$; $k[Z]/I_{m+1}$ is normal. For each even integer $0\le m\le t$, in the polynomial ring of a generic alternating $t\times t$ matrix $A$, the ideal $J_{m+2}$ generated by the principal Pfaffians of size $m+2$ is prime and its zero set is the locus $\operatorname{rank}A\le m$; $k[A]/J_{m+2}$ is normal. When the indicated generator size exceeds $t$, the corresponding ideal is zero and the quotient is polynomial.
thm-partition-diagram-orbit-basis-centra:
## Statement

Let $k$ be any field, $N\ge1$, and $r\ge0$, with the integer $N$ also denoting its scalar image in $k$. Let $W=k^N$ have basis $e_1,\ldots,e_N$, and let $S_N$ act by permuting this basis and diagonally on $W^{\otimes r}$. For a set partition diagram $d$ on the $2r$ boundary labels, define $\Phi(d)_{I,J}=1$ when all indices attached to vertices in each block of $d$ are equal, and $0$ otherwise; extend linearly. The partition algebra $P_r(N)$ from [[def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categories]] acts by $\Phi$, and its image is $\operatorname{End}_{S_N}(W^{\otimes r})$, the algebra of linear maps commuting with this action. Order set partitions by refinement: $d\preceq\pi$ means $\pi$ is a coarsening of $d$. Let $\mu(d,\pi)\in\mathbb Z$ be the inverse of the finite integer incidence matrix $\zeta(d,\pi)=1_{d\preceq\pi}$, and view these integers as scalars in $k$. Set $x_d=\sum_{\pi\succeq d}\mu(d,\pi)\,\pi$. Then $\Phi(x_d)$ is the indicator matrix of the exact equality pattern $d$ when $d$ has at most $N$ blocks, and is zero when $d$ has more than $N$ blocks. Consequently $\ker\Phi$ is the span of those $x_d$ with more than $N$ blocks, and $\Phi$ is injective exactly when $N\ge2r$. These statements hold even when $\operatorname{char}k$ divides $N!$.
lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation:
## Statement

Put $A=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},s,d^{\pm1}]/(s(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$. This ring is an integral domain and embeds in $\mathbb Q(i)(a,s)$ by $d\mapsto1+(a-a^{-1})/s$, where $i^2=-1$. A link diagram means a finite generic immersion of circles in the oriented plane with over/under data at its double points. Regular isotopy is generated by planar isotopy and Reidemeister moves II and III. A positive curl is a one-crossing curl whose oriented self-crossing has sign $+1$; its sign is independent of the direction chosen on its component. There is a unique function $P$ from link diagrams, including the empty diagram, to $A$ with $P(\varnothing)=1$, unchanged by regular isotopy, satisfying the following local rules: a positive or negative curl multiplies $P$ by $a$ or $a^{-1}$; a disjoint trivial circle multiplies $P$ by $d$; and $P(L_+)-P(L_-)=s(P(L_0)-P(L_\infty))$. Here in an oriented disk with four cyclically labelled endpoints $1,2,3,4$, $L_+$ connects $1$ to $3$ over the strand from $2$ to $4$, and the two smoothings are chosen so that the oriented smoothing for any orientation making this crossing positive is $L_0$; $L_-$ reverses the crossing and $L_\infty$ is the other smoothing. Rotating the disk interchanges both differences and preserves the rule. In particular the empty diagram freely generates the quotient of the free $A$-module on closed diagrams by these rules.
thm-bmw-kauffman-tangle-basis:
## Statement

Let $n\ge0$ and
$$R=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1},\rho^{\pm1},\delta^{\pm1}]/((q-q^{-1})(\delta-1)-(\rho-\rho^{-1})),\qquad z=q-q^{-1}.$$
Let $\Lambda_0=\mathbb Z[\lambda^{\pm1},z_0,\delta^{\pm1}]/(\lambda^{-1}-\lambda-z_0(\delta-1))$ and map it to $R$ by $\lambda\mapsto\rho$, $z_0\mapsto-z$, and $\delta\mapsto\delta$. A framed $(n,n)$ tangle is an isotopy class, fixing the boundary, of pairwise disjoint embedded ribbons in a rectangle times an interval, with $n$ prescribed ribbon intervals at each end. An ordinary $(n,n)$ tangle diagram is a generic immersed collection of arcs in the rectangle with those $2n$ fixed endpoints, with each transverse double point marked over/under. Regular isotopy means planar isotopy fixing the boundary together with Reidemeister moves II and III, but not move I; this is the framed-diagram convention of Goodman–Hauschild, §§2.1–2.2. Multiplication is vertical stacking, and the identity is the diagram of $n$ vertical strands. Define $KT_n(R)$ as the quotient of the free $R$-module on regular-isotopy classes by the local rules of Goodman–Hauschild, Definition 2.6, after the displayed parameter substitution: the crossing skein relation is $L_+-L_-=z(L_{\mathrm{id}}-L_{\mathrm{cup-cap}})$, the two opposite single-crossing curls evaluate to $\rho^{-1}$ and $\rho$ times the straight strand, and an isolated unknotted, untwisted circle is removed with coefficient $\delta$. Here $L_+$ and $L_-$ differ by the crossing, while $L_{\mathrm{id}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{cup-cap}}$ are its identity and cup-cap smoothings; all four diagrams agree outside a small disk. Order the $2n$ boundary labels by $1<\cdots<n<n'<\cdots<1'$. The standard orientation of a diagram orients each nonclosed strand from its lower-ordered endpoint to its higher-ordered endpoint and traverses the nonclosed strands by increasing initial endpoint. Such an oriented diagram is totally descending if every crossing is first met as an over-crossing in this traversal. For every perfect matching of the $2n$ boundary points there is a unique regular-isotopy class with that matching which is totally descending, has no strand self-crossings, and has no closed component. The universal BMW-to-tangle isomorphism over $\Lambda_0$ of Goodman–Hauschild, Theorem 5.41, base-changes along $\Lambda_0\to R$ to an isomorphism $BMW_n(R;q,\rho,\delta)\to KT_n(R)$ in the convention of [[def-bmw-algebra-with-fixed-kauffman-skein-convention]]. Both algebras are free over $R$ on these classes, so their rank is $(2n-1)!!$.
lem-gram-map-torsor-descent-and-codimens:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, let $V$ have dimension $m\ge1$ with a nondegenerate symmetric form or dimension $m=2n\ge2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form, and let $t\ge m+1$. On the full-rank locus of the rank-$\le m$ Gram variety, the Gram map from spanning tuples in $V^t$ is a principal bundle for the full orthogonal or symplectic group in the étale topology. Its regular invariant functions descend to regular functions on that locus. The omitted rank-$\le m-1$ symmetric stratum has codimension $t-m+1$, and the omitted rank-$\le m-2$ alternating stratum has codimension $2(t-m)+1$. Using normality of the rank varieties, each descended function extends uniquely across the omitted stratum.
lem-brauer-contraction-functor-and-bendi:
## Statement

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Let $V$ have dimension $m\ge1$ with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $B$ and $G=O(V,B):=\{g\in GL(V):B(gv,gw)=B(v,w)\}$, or dimension $m=2n\ge2$ with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form $B$ and $G=Sp(V,B):=\{g\in GL(V):B(gv,gw)=B(v,w)\}$; here $GL(V)$ is the group of invertible linear maps. Symmetric means $B(v,w)=B(w,v)$; alternating means $B(v,v)=0$ for every $v$; nondegenerate means $B(v,w)=0$ for every $w$ only when $v=0$. Put $\epsilon=1$ in the symmetric case and $\epsilon=-1$ in the alternating case. The assignments $I\mapsto\operatorname{id}_V$, $X\mapsto\epsilon P$ (where $P(v\otimes w)=w\otimes v$), $A\mapsto B$, and $U\mapsto c$ define the usual $G$-equivariant Brauer contraction maps at parameter $\delta=\epsilon m$. Bending gives a linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_G(V^{\otimes a},V^{\otimes b})\cong (V^{\otimes(a+b)})^G.$$
thm-orthogonal-and-symplectic-polynomial:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. For the full orthogonal group $O(V,B)$ of a nondegenerate symmetric $m$-dimensional space, the invariant ring $k[V^t]^{O(V,B)}$ is generated by $q_{ij}=B(v_i,v_j)$ and the kernel of $k[z_{ij}:i\le j]\to k[V^t]$, $z_{ij}\mapsto q_{ij}$, is the ideal of all $(m+1)$-minors of the generic symmetric Gram matrix. For the full symplectic group $Sp(V,\omega)$ of a nondegenerate alternating $2n$-dimensional space, $k[V^t]^{Sp(V,\omega)}$ is generated by $q_{ij}=\omega(v_i,v_j)$ for $i<j$, and the kernel of $k[a_{ij}:i<j]\to k[V^t]$ is generated by all principal Pfaffians of size $2n+2$ of the generic alternating Gram matrix. In both branches the claims concern the algebraic-group coaction invariants defined in [[def-polynomial-invariants-for-a-rational-linear-action]], not invariants under a finite subgroup of $G(k)$.
thm-orthogonal-and-symplectic-multilinea:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Let $V$ have dimension $m\ge1$ with a nondegenerate symmetric form and let $G=O(V)$, or let $\dim V=2n\ge2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form and let $G=Sp(V)$. For each $t\ge0$, identify the multidegree-$(1,\ldots,1)$ component of $k[V^t]^G$ with invariant multilinear forms on $t$ labelled vectors, using the form to identify $V$ with $V^*$. For a perfect matching, write every pair as $i<j$ and contract it as $B(v_i,v_j)$; this fixes the symplectic signs. For $t=2r$, these forms are spanned by the resulting pairwise contractions, one for each perfect matching of the labels; for odd $t$ the invariant space is zero. In the orthogonal case all relations among these contractions are generated by $(m+1)\times(m+1)$ Gram determinants on disjoint ordered label sets, multiplied by contractions on the remaining labels. In the symplectic case all relations are generated by Pfaffians of size $2n+2$ on label subsets, multiplied by contractions on the remaining labels. These contractions are linearly independent exactly when $r\le m$ for $O(V)$ and $r\le n$ for $Sp(V)$.
thm-brauer-orthogonal-symplectic-tensor-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $V$ be as in [[lem-brauer-contraction-functor-and-bending]]: dimension $m\ge1$ with a nondegenerate symmetric form and $G=O(V)$, or dimension $2n\ge2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form and $G=Sp(V)$. Use the full-group contraction functor from that item. For all nonnegative integers $a,b$, its image is $\operatorname{Hom}_G(V^{\otimes a},V^{\otimes b})$. Its kernel is the subspace obtained by bending the multilinear determinant relations of size $m+1$ in the orthogonal case, or the multilinear Pfaffian relations of size $2n+2$ in the symplectic case. In particular, the endomorphism map $B_r(\epsilon m)\to\operatorname{End}_G(V^{\otimes r})$ is surjective for every $r\ge0$ and is injective exactly when $r\le m$ for $O(V)$ or $r\le n$ for $Sp(V)$. The kernel in each fixed algebra is the span of all bent relations in that rank. The tensor ideal generated by these relations means the family of subspaces in all morphism spaces closed under composition on either side and tensoring by arbitrary diagrams. No reverse-commutant theorem is asserted here.
